items.title: It’s Time to Settle With Russia
items.summary: In October, U.S. President Donald Trump sold his eleventh-hour deal to secure diesel from Russian President Vladimir Putin—pausing sanctions that his own administration had imposed—as a boon for the negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. The arrangement, he wrote on Truth Social, was intended to keep Russia at “the bargaining table.” Of course, it was always obvious to observers that the gambit had as much or more to do with bolstering the U.S. economy and stemming a massive victory for the Democrats in this month’s midterm elections, and in that, it failed.Cynics have grounds for questioning all of Trump’s moves when it comes to Russia and Ukraine. He clearly dislikes Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and shows a marked preference for illiberal leaders, especially those willing to give him easy wins. Still, a stopped clock can be right twice a day. And concessions such as the fuel deal are exactly what might move Russia and Ukraine closer to peace, even if they are not wholly motivated by public-spiritedness.

items.title: The Ground Beneath the Cloud: Dispersion and Dependency in the Digital Age
items.summary:
Commercial cloud architecture has made digital infrastructure more resilient to localized disruption. Geographic dispersion, workload migration, and failover have allowed providers to preserve access in instances of degradation or even destruction. Yet, underpinning this resiliency are interlocking dependencies on access to energy, supply chains, and governing bodies that extend well beyond the data centers hosting the commercial cloud. items.title: Is Dollar Dominance in Decline?
items.summary:
The dominance of the U.S. dollar is a crucial source of American global power. The dollar’s widespread use, strength, and reliability provide major economic advantages for the United States, enable U.S. sanctions to have real bite, and significantly boost U.S. influence abroad. For America’s adversaries — as well as for many other countries that view Washington with some skepticism — dependence on the dollar comes with significant risks. Over the years, various proposals to develop rival alternatives have failed, demonstrating the depth of global reliance on the dollar.
